producerConsumerLaws.name: owned callback tables
producerConsumerLaws.law: Encoder initialization uses native immutable code/handler tables and typed owned callbacks, never original ROM application callback addresses. Generic request callers must supply their own owned tables. Model final patches do not assert native table addresses.

producerConsumerLaws.name: compact source bypass
producerConsumerLaws.law: The source-supported compact mode0/mode4 bypass updates the actual state and posts2b10. Normal branches execute preview and compression, not a substituted completion event.

producerConsumerLaws.name: channel8 completion
orderedEffects: Read and acknowledge the real hardware status.
Read processed-byte count only on the source ready branch.
Write size/error fields and compare the actual output-byte limit.
Invoke the registered source completion callback, which posts the real2b10 message.
The message consumer owns warp/channel cleanup, retry history and final caller notification.

producerConsumerLaws.name: quality and retry
producerConsumerLaws.law: Quality profile lookup is the JPEG-owned ROM algorithm. Owned polynomial scaling, clamped permutation-table quantization and retry history execute before owned warp/channel programming. Error/attempt fields determine retry versus final completion.

producerConsumerLaws.name: DMA channel lifecycle
orderedEffects: Reserve the actual channel semaphore and allocate a driver handle under the owned critical section.
Write arbitration and transfer registers in source order.
Register the owned completion callback and start actual DMA after the retained cache service.
Completion invokes the client callback, clears the global handle and releases IRQ, handle and semaphore state.

producerConsumerLaws.name: chunk writer
producerConsumerLaws.law: Template measurement and chunk/padding arithmetic execute owned CPU bodies. Template serialization executes JPEG-owned bodies. Payload transfer uses the owned DMA lifecycle, followed by the actual task notification/wait protocol, not a CPU copy or a scripted application completion.
